authority.human: selects account, contract, operating mode, and may submit manual intent
authority.hermes: owns probabilistic market judgment and trade intent
authority.glitch: owns truthful ProjectX evidence, identity, execution, protection, reconciliation, and receipts
authority.deterministic_rejection: limited to factual execution invalidity, authoritative venue/account boundaries, unprovable ownership or protection, duplicate or ambiguous mutation, and explicit operator disablement
authority.forbidden: hidden strategy gates, arbitrary risk preferences, trade creation without human or Hermes intent, and intent mutation outside the requested range

items.title: Bound runtime caches and prove stable heap under continuous trading
items.finding: Rearm states, all trade outcomes, and REST content hashes retain historical identities for the process lifetime.
resolution: Clear rearm state on tranche terminal and flat transitions.
Serve historical outcomes from SQLite with a bounded hot cache.
Apply active-identity scope or TTL/LRU to REST snapshot hashes.
Expose cache cardinality, eviction, and heap-slope metrics.
acceptance: Cardinality returns to documented bounds after positions close.
Recent outcome behavior remains correct without loading all history.
No reconciliation identity is evicted prematurely.
A multi-day synthetic soak shows stable post-GC heap slope.
deployment: Enable metrics first, choose conservative bounds from observation, soak in shadow, then tighten defaults.
items.implementation_note: Wave 1 (#210): MAX_HOT_OUTCOMES LRU in trade-outcome-store; rearmStates.clear on flat. Residual: provider-event-recorder hash bound, cache metrics, multi-day heap soak.
items.audit_2026_08_31_note: Re-verified 2026-08-31: all three named caches are now code-bounded, including the one item the 2026-08-27 implementation_note still listed as residual. (1) rearmStates (src/execution/coordinator.ts:96, a Map, out of this ticket's file scope but named directly in the finding) is cleared on every flat transition: coordinator.ts:967-971 rearmTrancheProtectionSerial clears this.rearmStates.clear() whenever snapshot.instrumentOpenContracts===0, and deletes the per-tranche entry on confirm (line 1007) -- matches resolution bullet 1 exactly. (2) trade outcomes: src/storage/trade-outcome-store.ts:5-6,174-179 MAX_HOT_OUTCOMES=2048 LRU eviction on the `known` Map, with SQLite (SqliteOutcomeFeed) as the authoritative store per the class comment at line 165 -- matches resolution bullet 2. (3) REST content hashes: src/projectx/provider-event-recorder.ts:46-47,94-107 ProviderRestSnapshotRecorder now has MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES=4096 with LRU eviction (rememberContentHash) and a cacheEvictions counter exposed via cacheMetrics(), which src/service.ts:571 surfaces as restEvidenceRecorder.cacheMetrics() in the health payload -- this was explicitly listed as residual in the 2026-08-27 note ('provider-event-recorder hash bound, cache metrics') and is now done, matching resolution bullets 3 and 4 (cardinality/eviction metrics exposed; heap-slope metric is not separately exposed). Remaining scoped gap, keeping this open: acceptance criterion 'A multi-day synthetic soak shows stable post-GC heap slope' has no evidence in docs/evidence/ -- this is a proof/soak deliverable, not a further code change (all three caches already have hard bounds), and it is the same class of residual work called out project-wide in the parent audit plan (Fase 0.4 / Fase 4 item 3: 72h PRAC soak never run). Downgrading is not warranted since the acceptance criterion is explicit and unmet, but the remaining work is narrowly the soak run itself, not new cache-bounding code. Separately, per this audit's scope note: src/execution/coordinator.ts is owned by a different audit slice (2.2) -- flagging only that rearmStates is confirmed already bounded above so that slice does not duplicate this investigation.

items.title: Require crash and fault injection before armed promotion
resolution: Add deterministic kill points around delivery, evidence, flatten, auth, and shutdown boundaries.
Inject 401/403/429, timeout, invalid JSON, ENOSPC, SQLite busy/corruption, stream lag, and process kill.
Assert paired restart convergence and emit immutable machine-readable proof.
Separate credential-free CI faults from sanitized Sim/PRAC evidence.
acceptance: Every critical re-audit scenario is red before correction and green after it.
Repeated faults converge without duplicate exposure or lost identity evidence.
Armed release rejects missing or stale fault proof.
deployment: Stabilize local/CI matrix, run shadow soak, execute approved Sim/PRAC subset, attach proof to the paired manifest.
items.implementation_note: Wave 1 (#210): intent-delivery-status.test.ts added to audit regression matrix file list. Residual: deterministic kill matrix CI gate, immutable fault proof JSON, release manifest enforcement.
items.audit_2026_08_31_note: Re-verified 2026-08-31: this is no longer accurately described as 'no matrix, only a file-list stub.' scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-gate.mjs runs a real set of fault-injection tests -- tests/kill-matrix.test.ts genuinely spawns a child process and delivers deterministic GLITCH_KILL_POINT signals across src/execution/kill-hook.ts KILL_POINTS, asserting no duplicate placeOrder calls and correct recovery (tests/kill-matrix.test.ts:1-100+); tests/reaudit-fault-matrix.test.ts covers auth_read_401_recovery and 429 mutation-no-retry; plus lifecycle-supervisor.test.ts, flatten-workflow.test.ts, gateway-shutdown-deadline.test.ts, sqlite-execution-store.test.ts, and the profile's tests/test_fault_injection.py (scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-proofs.json:1-21). The gate script emits an immutable, schema-versioned proof JSON (glitch.topstep.reaudit_fault_matrix_proof.v1) with per-file sha256 and gateway/profile commit SHAs (scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-gate.mjs:89-148), and IS wired as a required, verified step in .github/workflows/release.yml's paired-release-candidate workflow before the release artifact/manifest is built (release.yml:49-68 runs reaudit:fault-matrix then rejects a missing/mismatched profile_commit or malformed proof). Two real gaps remain, narrower than the original P0 framing: (1) this only runs on the manual workflow_dispatch armed-release path -- it is NOT in .github/workflows/ci.yml and NOT part of `npm run check` (package.json:13), so ordinary PR merges to main are not gated by it; (2) the proof bundle (scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-proofs.json) has no dedicated ENOSPC / SQLite-busy-or-corruption / stream-lag fault cases, though the resolution list called for them, and some disk-fault coverage exists elsewhere in the repo (e.g. TS-PROD-04 evidence) unlisted in this bundle. Downgraded P0->P1: the armed-release path is genuinely gated today; residual work is (a) add fault-matrix as a required check on every PR/push, not just manual release dispatch, and (b) extend the proof bundle to ENOSPC/SQLite-corruption/stream-lag scenarios.
items.closure_note: Fixed 2026-08-31 (plano-completo Fase 2.7.4). Core gap closed: the fault-matrix gate (scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-gate.mjs, already a real kill-point/lifecycle/auth-backoff test runner, not a stub) previously only ran on the manual paired-release-candidate workflow. .github/workflows/ci.yml now has a fault-matrix job that runs on every push/PR, checking out glitch-topstep-hermes-profile@main alongside this repo and uploading the versioned proof JSON as a CI artifact -- verified end to end locally (ran npm run reaudit:fault-matrix against both real repos, gateway_commit + profile_commit + per-file sha256 all captured correctly). scripts/reaudit-fault-matrix-proofs.json extended with the 4 new/extended test files from this session's other fixes (protection.test.ts, protection-supervisor.test.ts, read-circuit-breaker.test.ts, intent-delivery-status.test.ts) so EX-01/EX-02/PX-01/REAUDIT-04's regression coverage is part of the gated proof bundle, not just the local test suite. Deferred, explicitly not attempted this session: ENOSPC, SQLite busy, and SQLite corruption fault-injection cases. These need new test infrastructure (real disk-full and lock-contention simulation) rather than extending an existing file, and rushing that under time pressure risked flaky, low-confidence coverage -- better as a dedicated follow-up than a rushed addition here. Stream-lag fault behavior is already covered by the existing 'SignalR stream supervisor' test suite (not part of this ticket's original ask, already adequate).
items.post_review_note: Downgraded from 'done' 2026-08-31 after an external post-implementation review correctly pointed out this ticket's own closure_note already listed unmet gaps (ENOSPC/SQLite-busy/SQLite-corruption fault cases explicitly deferred) that should have kept it out of 'done'. The original 2026-08-27 finding ('no matrix, only a file-list stub') IS resolved -- a real fault-injection gate exists and now runs on every push/PR (ci.yml fault-matrix job, verified end-to-end locally against both real repos, gateway/profile SHAs both captured in a freshly-regenerated release/reaudit-fault-matrix-proof.json). What is NOT done: the disk/SQLite fault cases the 2026-08-31 plan's fuller ask (Fase 2 section 7.4) explicitly listed. Reclassifying honestly as in_progress rather than claiming full closure against the expanded ask.

items.title: ProjectX stream recovery — hub liveness vs execution quality
items.finding: Gateway flapping degraded: ~1489 market_liveness_restart with depth/trade traffic; 15s quote-only liveness; overlapping SignalR restartHub + watchdog process kill; burst REST on reconnect. Not duplicate ProjectX clients on operator machine.
resolution: Separate hub_liveness (any market event + SignalR state) from execution_quality (quote freshness, geometry, contract match).
Debounce liveness restarts; recovery_generation; HubRecoveryController per hub (market first).
Serial reconnect pipeline: resubscribe → reconcile → observation → history.
Transport-error retry with global deadline for idempotent reads; reconcile cheap cycle (positions/orders).
Health recovery progress fields; watchdog kills only on stale progress past deadline.
Scheduler and persistence optimization in follow-up PRs after 72h PRAC soak.
acceptance: market_liveness_restart drops >80% in stable RTH over 24h after PR-A/B.
Watchdog restarts <1/hour RTH outside maintenance; causes tagged in log.
ENTER gates unchanged: quote_stale and state_complete still block new exposure.
npm run check and reaudit fault matrix green.
72h PRAC soak evidence with session-conditioned metrics.
items.implementation_note: Plan authored 2026-08-27 from operational flap 2026-08-26 EDT + code audit. PR order: A hub/debounce → B recovery controller → C retry → D serial reconnect → E watchdog progress → soak 72h → F–H scheduler/persistence. Do not use GLITCH_STREAM_LIVENESS_MS=60000 in armed without controlled experiment. PR-A–E implemented 2026-08-27 locally; pending 72h PRAC soak for acceptance.
items.audit_2026_08_31_note: Confirmed 2026-08-31: no docs/evidence/PRAC-SOAK-2026-08-27* or later file exists (docs/evidence/ only has PRAC-SOAK-2026-08-21-single-active-position.md and PRAC-SOAK-2026-08-25-post-audit-wave.md) -- the 72h PRAC soak this item's own acceptance criteria requires was never run. A fresh flapping recurrence occurred 2026-08-31 (61 restarts). This recurrence is evidence the soak gate was correctly withheld: PR-A-E were 'implemented, not proven,' and shipping them to continuous unattended autostart before the soak completed would not have caught this regression either. Do not close this item and do not treat PR-A-E as sufficient. PR-F (scheduler unification replacing the 4 independent timers) was never started: src/projectx/rest-concurrency.ts:1 still carries the exact comment 'ponytail: global REST gate — upgrade path is priority scheduler (PR-F)' and RestConcurrencyGate (rest-concurrency.ts:2-19) remains a simple counting semaphore with a FIFO waiter queue, not a priority scheduler; no other file in src/ references PR-F. The 4 timers PR-F is meant to unify are confirmed still independent and uncoordinated in src/service.ts: reconcile every this.config.reconcileIntervalMs (default 3000ms via GLITCH_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, src/config.ts:474), set up at src/service.ts:457-462; history sync every this.historySyncIntervalMs (default 60_000ms, src/service.ts:83/189, src/config.ts:293), set up at src/service.ts:467-472; market observation every MARKET_OBSERVATION_REFRESH_MS=60_000 (src/service.ts:85), set up at src/service.ts:480-483; order flow every ORDER_FLOW_REFRESH_MS=10_000 (src/service.ts:88), set up at src/service.ts:488-491. Each is its own unref'd setInterval with no shared scheduler, no priority ordering, and no coordination with the others or with REST concurrency pressure. PR-G (adaptive reconcile) and PR-H (persistence/health tuning for DB ~500MB+) were also never started -- no references anywhere in src/. Status stays in_progress; remaining work is unchanged in scope (72h PRAC soak, then PR-F/G/H) but now has direct 2026-08-31 evidence that skipping the soak gate would have been the wrong call.
items.audit_2026_08_31_pr_fgh_note: PR-F/G/H implemented 2026-08-31 (plano-completo Fase 3, at the user's explicit request despite the size/risk, since the 72h soak can't be run by this session either way -- STILL UNSOAKED, do not treat as trusted for continuous armed operation). PR-F: src/service/task-scheduler.ts (new, 7 unit tests) -- a TaskScheduler coordinates the four previously fully-independent setInterval callbacks (reconcile, market observation, order flow, history sync). Each timer keeps its exact original cadence; the scheduler only bounds concurrency (maxConcurrent=2), enforces priority order (critical_reconcile > market_recovery > market_observation > order_flow > history_sync), coalesces duplicate pending requests by id, and has a starvation guard (a task past its own deadline is promoted ahead of nominally higher-priority newcomers). Wired into AppService via a persistent instance; counts exposed at /health task_scheduler; hooked into shutdown's waitForIdle drain. Does not touch quote_stale/state_complete entry gates. PR-G: investigation found the 'cheap vs full reconcile cycle' ask was already implemented (shouldReconcileMetadata/RECONCILE_METADATA_INTERVAL_MS predate this session). Added the one genuine gap: bounded jittered backoff on repeated reconcile failures (reuses the already-tested projectXAuthBackoffDelayMs from TS-REAUDIT-01 -- generic despite the name), so a persistent ProjectX outage can't turn the reconcile timer into a tight failure loop. NOT implemented: 'higher frequency during recovery' -- judged too invasive to the core reconcile timing to add safely in this pass; left for a dedicated change. PR-H: added persistence_bytes (per-store SQLite file size via fs.statSync, never throws), heap_used_bytes (process.memoryUsage().heapUsed), and health_build_ms (wall-clock time to build the /health response) to the /health payload. Did NOT instrument SQLite-internal latency/busy-lock/fsync timing -- that needs wrapping every prepare()/run() call across many files, a materially larger and more invasive change than this pass's risk budget allowed. Testability note: TaskScheduler is fully unit-tested in isolation (pure class, injectable clock). The reconcile-backoff wiring and persistenceSizeBytes() are NOT independently unit-tested -- AppService has no test harness anywhere in this repo (nothing constructs it directly; it wires SignalR/SQLite/HTTP), so this specific glue code relies on the full npm run check suite (532/532 green) plus manual code review, not a dedicated test. 72h PRAC soak remains the sole path to trusting any of this under continuous armed operation -- unchanged from the ticket's existing acceptance criteria.
items.post_review_note: 2026-08-31, same session: an external post-implementation review correctly found that the first PR-F commit only routed the four periodic setInterval timers through TaskScheduler -- handleHubReconnected (the post-reconnect recovery pipeline, the EXACT scenario PR-F exists to fix) still called reconcile/refreshMarketObservations/orderFlow.refresh/historySync.sync directly, fully bypassing the scheduler. Fixed: TaskScheduler.enqueue() now returns the task's own result as a promise (was void/fire-and-forget), so handleHubReconnected awaits each step through the scheduler at 'market_recovery' priority using the SAME task ids as the periodic timers -- a concurrent periodic tick and a recovery run wanting the same work now coalesce into one REST call. Coalescing also upgrades a queued task to the best priority any waiting caller asked for. 6 new tests cover this. Also fixed a related bug the API change surfaced: two fire-and-forget periodic call sites needed an explicit .catch() to avoid an unhandled promise rejection once enqueue() started returning a promise. See commit faae372.
items.post_review_note_2: Second review round, 2026-08-31 same session. Terminology correction: PR-F is precisely a COORDINATED DISPATCH LAYER, not a replacement of the timer trigger sources. The four setInterval calls (and the reconnect event) still independently decide WHEN to request work; TaskScheduler decides the ORDER and CONCURRENCY of the resulting REST-bound execution. If a fully centralized trigger source (a single scheduler owning cadence too, not just dispatch) is later judged necessary, that is materially more invasive and explicitly out of scope for this pass. Coalescing-vs-running-task behavior is now an explicit, tested, documented decision (queued-only coalescing; a same-id request during an in-flight run gets a fresh sequential run, never a stale shared result) -- see TaskScheduler's class doc and tests/task-scheduler.test.ts. Added one real disk fault case (SQLite busy/lock contention, tests/sqlite-busy-fault.test.ts) confirming contention is a catchable, recoverable condition against the real driver and pragmas -- ENOSPC and corruption remain unattempted. Still genuinely missing, unchanged: an AppService-level integration test exercising the real timer objects + handleHubReconnected + TaskScheduler together (periodic tick, reconnect, coalescing across both, task failure, a second recovery generation, shutdown mid-task) -- AppService has no test harness in this repo and building one is a separate, larger undertaking than this session's remaining scope. PR-H runtime instrumentation (SQLite internal write/fsync latency, not just the fault-injection proof added here) also remains unimplemented, as previously noted.
